words.enDefinition: The study of relationships between physical stimuli and sensory experience.

examples.en: In psychophysics, we can ask how changes in light intensity affect the brightness people report.
examples.zh: 在「心理物理学」中，我们可以研究光强变化如何影响人们报告的亮度。

examples.en: The opening psychophysics lecture compared physical sound level with the loudness listeners reported in class.
examples.zh: 「心理物理学」的第一堂课对比了声音的物理声级与听者报告的响度。

words.enDefinition: The stimulus level detected at a specified rate, conventionally half the time.

examples.en: Our class estimated the absolute threshold where observers detected the target in half the presentations.
examples.zh: 在一半试次能检出目标的位置，我们估计出了「绝对阈限」。

examples.en: The absolute threshold in the worksheet was lower against the quieter of the two backgrounds.
examples.zh: 习题中，较安静的背景对应较低的「绝对阈限」。

words.enDefinition: The smallest stimulus difference reliably discriminated at a stated performance level.

examples.en: We estimated the difference threshold for brightness using ratings from a simulated classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 我们用课堂模拟练习中的评分估计了亮度的「差别阈限」。

examples.en: The graph showed a higher difference threshold for pitch at the higher of the two reference frequencies.
examples.zh: 图中，在两个参照频率中较高的那一个，音高的「差别阈限」也较高。

words.enDefinition: The approximate rule that detectable increments scale with the starting stimulus magnitude.

examples.en: Weber's law predicts that the heavier reference object requires a larger increase to feel different.
examples.zh: 「韦伯定律」预测，参照物体越重，就需要增加更多重量才能感觉到不同。

examples.en: The lecturer used Weber's law to explain why the ratio mattered in that range.
examples.zh: 老师用「韦伯定律」解释了为什么在这个范围内要看比值。

words.enDefinition: The ratio of a difference threshold to its reference stimulus magnitude.

examples.en: The example divided the weight increment by the reference weight to obtain the Weber fraction.
examples.zh: 例题将重量增量除以参照重量，得到了「韦伯分数」。

examples.en: Our two examples gave similar values for the Weber fraction despite using different reference weights.
examples.zh: 尽管参照重量不同，两道例题算出的「韦伯分数」相近。

collocations: compare estimates of the Weber fraction

words.enDefinition: The model in which sensation magnitude grows logarithmically with stimulus intensity.

examples.en: The curve from Fechner's law rises slowly even when the intensity increases by a large amount.
examples.zh: 即使刺激强度增加很多，「费希纳定律」给出的曲线也只缓慢上升。

examples.en: In the reading, Fechner's law described sensation magnitude on a different scale from physical intensity.
examples.zh: 阅读材料中的「费希纳定律」用不同于物理强度的尺度描述感觉量。

collocations: a curve predicted by Fechner's law

words.enDefinition: A model relating sensation magnitude to a power of stimulus intensity.

examples.en: Stevens' power law allowed the two example judgments to follow curves with different exponents.
examples.zh: 「史蒂文斯幂定律」允许用指数不同的曲线表示两种示例判断。

examples.en: The instructor compared Stevens' power law with a logarithmic model on the same classroom plot.
examples.zh: 老师在同一幅课堂图中比较了「史蒂文斯幂定律」与对数模型。

collocations: a prediction from Stevens' power law
the exponent in Stevens' power law

words.enDefinition: A curve linking stimulus magnitude to the probability of a particular perceptual response.

examples.en: We fitted a psychometric function to show how detection responses changed as the tones grew louder.
examples.zh: 我们拟合了「心理测量函数」，展示音调变响时检测作答如何变化。

examples.en: The psychometric function was shallower for the simulated listener whose judgments varied more across trials.
examples.zh: 在各次试验中判断波动较大的模拟听者，对应的「心理测量函数」曲线更平缓。

collocations: the slope of a psychometric function

words.enDefinition: An approach estimating a threshold from ordered increasing and decreasing stimulus series.

examples.en: For the method of limits, the handout graphed trials in both increasing and decreasing intensity order.
examples.zh: 讲义把「极限法」中按强度递增和递减呈现的试次分别画了出来。

examples.en: The example marked where responses changed during each series in the method of limits.
examples.zh: 示例在「极限法」的每个序列中标出了作答发生变化的位置。

collocations: estimate a threshold using the method of limits
an ascending sequence in the method of limits
compare the method of limits with constant stimuli

words.enDefinition: An approach in which observers directly vary a stimulus to meet a perceptual criterion.

examples.en: In the method of adjustment, the classroom observer changed a patch until its brightness matched the reference.
examples.zh: 课堂展示「调整法」时，观察者调整色块，直到它跟参照色块看起来一样亮。

examples.en: The method of adjustment let observers control the comparison stimulus in the example on the slide.
examples.zh: 投影片的示例中，「调整法」让观察者自行控制比较刺激。

collocations: a threshold from the method of adjustment
a brightness match using the method of adjustment

words.enDefinition: An approach presenting fixed stimulus levels repeatedly, typically in randomized order.

examples.en: In the method of constant stimuli, the worksheet listed the same intensity levels in a shuffled sequence.
examples.zh: 习题将相同的几个强度水平打乱呈现，展示了「恒定刺激法」。

examples.en: We plotted the response proportions for the method of constant stimuli using the simulated class data.
examples.zh: 我们用课堂模拟数据画出了「恒定刺激法」下各作答的比例。

collocations: a threshold from the method of constant stimuli
fixed levels in the method of constant stimuli
use the method of constant stimuli

words.enDefinition: A procedure adjusting stimulus levels according to earlier observer responses.

examples.en: In the simulated adaptive staircase, the next level depended on whether the previous answer was correct.
examples.zh: 在模拟的「自适应阶梯法」中，下一档取决于前一次作答是否正确。

examples.en: The lecture traced each reversal in an adaptive staircase with a different mark on the chart.
examples.zh: 老师在图中用不同的记号标出了「自适应阶梯法」每次改变增减方向的位置。

words.enDefinition: A task design requiring a response from two specified alternatives on every trial.

examples.en: Our two-alternative forced choice example asked which of two intervals contained the faint tone.
examples.zh: 我们的「二选一迫选」示例要求判断微弱音调出现在哪一个时段。

examples.en: In the two-alternative forced choice task, a guess still counted as one of the two options.
examples.zh: 在「二选一迫选」任务中，即使靠猜，作答也只能从两个选项中选一个。

words.enDefinition: A task asking whether a signal was present on each trial.

examples.en: The yes-no detection task included silent trials as well as trials containing a brief tone.
examples.zh: 「是否检出任务」既有静默试次，也有播放短音的试次。

examples.en: In the simulated yes-no detection task, responses were recorded separately for each type of trial.
examples.zh: 在模拟「是否检出任务」中，不同类型试次的作答分别记录。

collocations: a yes-no detection task with tones
responses in a yes-no detection task
compare a yes-no detection task with forced choice

words.enDefinition: A framework separating detection sensitivity from the criterion for reporting a signal.

examples.en: Signal detection theory explained why two observers with similar hearing sensitivity sometimes gave different answers.
examples.zh: 「信号检测理论」解释了为何听觉敏感性相近的两名观察者有时会给出不同回答。

examples.en: The seminar used signal detection theory to distinguish better discrimination from a willingness to answer yes.
examples.zh: 讨论课运用「信号检测理论」区分了辨别力提高和更倾向于回答检出。

collocations: a model from signal detection theory
an introduction to signal detection theory

words.enDefinition: A detection trial in which the target signal is actually present.

examples.en: The faint tone made that example a signal-present trial even though the listener answered no.
examples.zh: 听者虽然回答没有，但这一试次确实播放了微弱音调，所以属于「有信号试次」。

examples.en: We marked each signal-present trial using the stimulus record before looking at the simulated responses.
examples.zh: 我们根据刺激记录标出每个「有信号试次」，再看模拟作答。

collocations: a response on a signal-present trial

words.enDefinition: A detection trial containing background activity without the target signal.

examples.en: The recording contained only background noise during the signal-absent trial illustrated on the classroom slide.
examples.zh: 课堂投影片展示的「无信号试次」中，录音里只有背景噪声。

examples.en: Our worksheet included a signal-absent trial with a yes response to illustrate a false alarm.
examples.zh: 我们的习题用回答有信号的「无信号试次」来说明什么是虚报。

collocations: a response on a signal-absent trial
a correct response on a signal-absent trial

words.enDefinition: The ability to distinguish a stimulus or signal from alternatives or background noise.

examples.en: The simulated listeners had similar perceptual sensitivity despite using different criteria for reporting the faint tone.
examples.zh: 两位模拟听者报告微弱音调的标准不同，「知觉敏感性」却相近。

examples.en: We compared perceptual sensitivity across the two noise conditions instead of counting only positive responses.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两种噪声条件下的「知觉敏感性」，没有只统计回答检出的次数。

words.enDefinition: A measure of separation between noise and signal-plus-noise distributions in the standard signal detection model.

examples.en: The lecturer used d-prime to compare discrimination in two sets of hypothetical detection responses.
examples.zh: 老师用「检测辨别力指数」比较两组假想检测作答所显示的辨别力。

examples.en: In the example, d-prime increased when the two modeled distributions became more clearly separated.
examples.zh: 例题中，两个模型分布之间的间隔越明显，「检测辨别力指数」就越高。

words.enDefinition: The internal cutoff for deciding which response to give in a task.

examples.en: The classroom model illustrated how a stricter response criterion reduced both hits and false alarms.
examples.zh: 课堂模型展示了更严格的「反应判准」如何同时减少命中和虚报。

examples.en: We drew the response criterion as a vertical line across the two simulated evidence distributions.
examples.zh: 我们在两个模拟证据分布上画出一条竖线，表示「反应判准」。

words.enDefinition: A systematic tendency to favor one response apart from perceptual sensitivity.

examples.en: The two groups showed different response bias even though their discrimination scores were nearly identical.
examples.zh: 两组的辨别得分几乎一样，却显示出不同的「反应偏向」。

examples.en: In the classroom analysis, response bias described how readily the simulated listener reported hearing a signal.
examples.zh: 在课堂分析中，「反应偏向」描述模拟听者有多倾向于报告听到信号。

words.enDefinition: The proportion of signal-present trials correctly answered with a signal report.

examples.en: We calculated the hit rate using only trials that actually contained the faint classroom tone.
examples.zh: 我们只统计确实播放了课堂微弱音调的试次，计算「命中率」。

examples.en: A higher hit rate did not settle which simulated listener was more sensitive in the example.
examples.zh: 在例题中，更高的「命中率」无法单独确定哪位模拟听者更敏感。

words.enDefinition: The proportion of signal-present trials answered as though no signal was present.

examples.en: The simulated listener had a lower miss rate when the target tone stood out more clearly.
examples.zh: 目标音调更突出时，模拟听者的「漏报率」较低。

examples.en: Our worksheet calculated the miss rate from negative responses on trials that contained the signal.
examples.zh: 习题根据实际有信号时回答未检出的次数计算「漏报率」。

words.enDefinition: The proportion of signal-absent trials on which a signal is reported.

examples.en: The class computed the false alarm rate from yes responses in trials containing only background sound.
examples.zh: 全班根据仅有背景声却回答有信号的试次，计算了「虚报率」。

examples.en: The model produced a higher false alarm rate when observers accepted weaker evidence for a signal.
examples.zh: 观察者根据较弱证据也会报告存在信号时，模型给出的「虚报率」较高。

words.enDefinition: The proportion of signal-absent trials correctly answered with a no-signal report.

examples.en: We used the correct rejection rate to summarize how often listeners correctly answered no during silent trials.
examples.zh: 我们用「正确拒绝率」概括听者在静默试次中正确回答无信号的频率。

examples.en: Our class table compared the correct rejection rate with the false alarm rate for trials without a signal.
examples.zh: 课堂表格比较了无信号试次的「正确拒绝率」和虚报率。

words.enDefinition: Performance expected from guessing under the stated task conditions.

examples.en: The dashed line showed chance performance for the classroom task with two equally likely answers.
examples.zh: 课堂任务中两个答案同样可能，虚线表示「随机猜测水平」。

examples.en: We compared the simulated group's accuracy with chance performance before interpreting the small apparent advantage.
examples.zh: 解释看起来很小的优势之前，我们先把模拟小组的正确率与「随机猜测水平」对比。

collocations: compare an accuracy score with chance performance

words.enDefinition: The comparison stimulus value perceived as equal to a reference on average.

examples.en: We marked the point of subjective equality where the two patches were judged equally bright overall.
examples.zh: 我们标出「主观等同点」，即总体上两块色块被判断为一样亮的位置。

examples.en: The point of subjective equality shifted when the simulated brightness comparison included a darker surround.
examples.zh: 模拟亮度比较采用较暗背景时，「主观等同点」发生了偏移。

collocations: estimate the point of subjective equality
a shift in the point of subjective equality
plot the point of subjective equality

words.enDefinition: An approach asking observers to assign numbers proportional to perceived intensity.

examples.en: In the magnitude estimation example, participants assigned larger numbers to tones they judged much louder.
examples.zh: 在「数量估计法」示例中，参与者给听起来响得多的音调分配了更大的数值。

examples.en: We plotted classroom magnitude estimation responses against the physical intensity values listed on the slide.
examples.zh: 我们用投影片列出的物理强度值和课堂「数量估计法」的作答绘图。

words.enDefinition: A stimulus above the specified sensory threshold under stated conditions.

examples.en: One suprathreshold stimulus on the demonstration graph fell well above the estimated detection level.
examples.zh: 演示图上的一个「阈上刺激」远高于估计的检测水平。

examples.en: The instructor used a suprathreshold stimulus to discuss differences in appearance after detection became reliable.
examples.zh: 老师用一个「阈上刺激」讨论可靠检出以后仍能感知到的外观差异。

words.enDefinition: Processing of stimuli below a specified threshold for conscious awareness.

examples.en: The seminar discussed subliminal perception and asked how the fictional study assessed awareness of the image.
examples.zh: 讨论课以「阈下知觉」为主题，并追问虚构研究是怎样检验受试者是否察觉图像的。

examples.en: Our notes separated evidence for subliminal perception from claims about lasting effects on behavior.
examples.zh: 我们的笔记区分了「阈下知觉」的证据和关于持久影响行为的说法。

words.enDefinition: The arrangement of sensory information into coherent objects and patterns.

examples.en: The slides illustrated perceptual organization by rearranging the same dots into several apparently different patterns.
examples.zh: 投影片把同样的圆点重新排列，使人看出几种不同的图案，借此说明「知觉组织」。

examples.en: Our discussion of perceptual organization began with a drawing whose foreground and background looked equally plausible.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「知觉组织」时，先看了一幅前景与背景都同样说得通的图。

words.enDefinition: The experience of distinct elements as members of a common perceptual unit.

examples.en: The Gestalt demonstration showed perceptual grouping when students saw rows instead of a collection of individual dots.
examples.zh: 格式塔演示中，学生看到一排排的圆点，这个例子展示了「知觉分组」。

examples.en: The handout used changes in spacing and shape to illustrate two cues for perceptual grouping.
examples.zh: 讲义用间距和形状的变化说明两种「知觉分组」线索。

words.enDefinition: General tendencies governing how people group elements and organize perceptual scenes.

examples.en: We used the Gestalt principles of perception to explain why the same dots formed different groups.
examples.zh: 我们用「格式塔知觉原则」解释为何同样的圆点形成了不同分组。

examples.en: The tutor reviewed the Gestalt principles of perception before showing a drawing with an ambiguous foreground.
examples.zh: 辅导老师先复习「格式塔知觉原则」，再展示一幅前景难以确定的图。

collocations: examples of Gestalt principles of perception

words.enDefinition: The perceptual separation of a figure from the background against which it appears.

examples.en: The first image illustrated figure-ground organization because the dark shape stood out against the pale surrounding area.
examples.zh: 第一幅图中的深色形状在浅色区域的衬托下显得突出，说明了「图形与背景组织」。

examples.en: We discussed figure-ground organization after seeing how a single border could belong to either adjacent region.
examples.zh: 看到同一条边界可以归属任一相邻区域后，我们讨论了「图形与背景组织」。

words.enDefinition: An alternation in perception that exchanges which region is figure and which is ground.

examples.en: The vase drawing showed figure-ground reversal when two dark profiles became the figure instead of the vase.
examples.zh: 花瓶图中，两个深色侧脸取代花瓶成为主体，展示了「图形背景反转」。

examples.en: Several students reported a figure-ground reversal even though the picture itself stayed unchanged on the screen.
examples.zh: 尽管屏幕上的图没有变化，几名学生仍报告看到了「图形背景反转」。

words.enDefinition: The tendency to group elements that are close together in space.

examples.en: The law of proximity explained why the closely spaced marks looked like pairs in the diagram.
examples.zh: 「接近律」解释了为什么图上相距较近的记号看起来成双成对。

examples.en: Our instructor showed the law of proximity by changing the spacing while keeping every mark identical.
examples.zh: 老师让记号本身保持一致，只调整间距，以展示「接近律」。

collocations: an example of the law of proximity
grouping by the law of proximity

words.enDefinition: The tendency to group elements with similar perceptual features.

examples.en: The law of similarity explained why students grouped circles by color even when all distances matched.
examples.zh: 「相似律」解释了为什么圆点间距一致时，学生仍按颜色分组。

examples.en: In the figure, the law of similarity made the repeating triangles look separate from the surrounding circles.
examples.zh: 在图中，根据「相似律」，重复出现的三角形看起来与周围的圆形分属不同组。

collocations: an example of the law of similarity
grouping by the law of similarity

words.enDefinition: The tendency to perceive incomplete elements as forming a complete shape.

examples.en: The broken ring illustrated the law of closure because students still saw a single complete shape.
examples.zh: 轮廓有缺口的圆环说明了「闭合律」，因为学生仍把它看成一个完整形状。

examples.en: Our example of the law of closure used several gaps that did not prevent recognition of the square.
examples.zh: 我们用有几个缺口的正方形来展示「闭合律」，这些缺口并未妨碍识别。

collocations: grouping under the law of closure
an example of the law of closure

words.enDefinition: The tendency to group edge segments forming a smooth path.

examples.en: The crossing lines demonstrated good continuation because the smooth paths looked like two uninterrupted strokes.
examples.zh: 交叉线条说明了「良好连续原则」，因为两条平滑走向各自看起来都是连贯的一笔。

examples.en: We discussed good continuation after comparing a smooth path with an abrupt turn at the crossing.
examples.zh: 在交叉点比较了平缓路径和急转弯后，我们讨论了「良好连续原则」。

words.enDefinition: The tendency to group elements moving or changing together.

examples.en: The moving dots illustrated common fate when those traveling in the same direction looked like one group.
examples.zh: 动画里的圆点朝同一方向移动时看起来像一组，展示了「共同命运原则」。

examples.en: We contrasted common fate with similarity using dots of the same color that moved in different directions.
examples.zh: 课堂展示了同色圆点朝不同方向移动，用以区分「共同命运原则」和相似律。

words.enDefinition: The tendency to group elements enclosed within the same area.

examples.en: The diagram illustrated common region by placing two different shapes inside the same faint border.
examples.zh: 这幅图把两种不同的形状放进同一个浅色边框，以展示「共同区域原则」。

examples.en: In the example of common region, widely separated dots looked related because they shared a shaded background.
examples.zh: 在「共同区域原则」示例中，相距很远的圆点共用一块阴影背景，因此显得有关联。

words.enDefinition: The tendency to perceive connected elements within a uniform region as one unit.

examples.en: The slide illustrated uniform connectedness by linking distant dots with lines of the same color.
examples.zh: 投影片用同色线条连接相隔很远的圆点，以展示「一致连接原则」。

examples.en: Uniform connectedness helped explain why the linked shapes looked more unified than some much closer pairs.
examples.zh: 「一致连接原则」有助于解释为何连起来的形状看起来比某些离得近得多的成对形状更像一个整体。

words.enDefinition: A perceived edge lacking a corresponding physical boundary in the stimulus.

examples.en: The classroom triangle produced an illusory contour where there was no line drawn on the page.
examples.zh: 课堂上的三角形图案在纸上未画线的位置产生了「主观轮廓」。

examples.en: Students traced an illusory contour around the white region even though its brightness never changed along that edge.
examples.zh: 即使白色区域在那条边两侧的亮度一样，学生仍描出了它的「主观轮廓」。

words.enDefinition: Perceiving a partly hidden object as complete without seeing its concealed parts.

examples.en: Amodal completion made the two visible pieces look like one bar continuing behind the square.
examples.zh: 「非模态补全」使看得见的两部分像是同一根长条，在方形后面连在一起。

examples.en: In the amodal completion drawing, students recognized a circle while only part of its outline was visible.
examples.zh: 「非模态补全」图中，学生只看见部分轮廓，却认出了一个圆。

words.enDefinition: Perceiving stable properties despite changes in the sensory information reaching the observer.

examples.en: The lecture introduced perceptual constancy by showing the same objects under changes in viewpoint and illumination.
examples.zh: 课堂通过展示视角和光照改变时的同一批物体，引入了「知觉恒常性」。

examples.en: Perceptual constancy explained why the classroom display still looked stable as the simulated observer moved around it.
examples.zh: 「知觉恒常性」解释了为什么模拟观察者走动时，课堂展示中的物体看起来仍然稳定。

words.enDefinition: Perceiving an object's size as stable across changes in viewing distance.

examples.en: The size constancy slide showed why a receding object need not appear physically smaller to the viewer.
examples.zh: 「大小恒常性」投影片说明，物体逐渐远去时，观察者感知的实际大小不一定变小。

examples.en: We discussed size constancy after comparing pictures of the same box at two different distances.
examples.zh: 我们比较了同一个盒子在不同距离拍摄的两张照片，然后讨论了「大小恒常性」。

words.enDefinition: Perceiving an object's shape as stable across changes in viewing angle.

examples.en: The instructor used shape constancy to explain why an angled door still looked rectangular in the video.
examples.zh: 老师用「形状恒常性」解释为什么视频中侧着看的门仍显得是长方形。

examples.en: Shape constancy mattered in the example even though the outline on the screen changed with the camera angle.
examples.zh: 虽然屏幕上的轮廓随拍摄角度改变，例子中的「形状恒常性」仍然起了作用。

words.enDefinition: Perceiving a surface's color as relatively stable under different illumination.

examples.en: The color constancy example showed that the blue folder could look blue under two different lights.
examples.zh: 「颜色恒常性」示例表明，同一个蓝色文件夹在两种光照下都可能看起来是蓝色的。

examples.en: We discussed color constancy by comparing images of the same surface photographed under different light sources.
examples.zh: 我们比较同一表面在不同光源下拍摄的图像，讨论了「颜色恒常性」。

words.enDefinition: Perceiving a surface as reflecting a similar proportion of light under different illumination.

examples.en: Lightness constancy explained why the white paper still looked white in the shaded part of the demonstration.
examples.zh: 「明度恒常性」解释了为什么演示中处于阴影里的白纸看起来仍是白色。

examples.en: The shadow example illustrated lightness constancy even though the two paper patches sent different amounts of light back.
examples.zh: 尽管两块纸片反射的光量不同，这个阴影示例仍展示了「明度恒常性」。

words.enDefinition: Information from both eyes that contributes to perceiving relative depth.

examples.en: The paired drawings provided a binocular depth cue even though the screen itself was perfectly flat.
examples.zh: 虽然屏幕是平的，这对图仍提供了「双眼深度线索」。

examples.en: The lecturer contrasted a binocular depth cue with shading information available in a single flat image.
examples.zh: 老师将一种「双眼深度线索」与单张平面图像中已有的阴影信息作了对比。

collocations: a binocular depth cue in stereopsis

words.enDefinition: The difference in corresponding image locations on the two retinas.

examples.en: The diagram showed retinal disparity by comparing where the same point appeared in the two eye images.
examples.zh: 示意图对比同一点在两眼图像中的位置，从而展示「视网膜视差」。

examples.en: In the classroom example, changing retinal disparity made one part of the image appear nearer than another.
examples.zh: 在课堂示例中，改变「视网膜视差」使图像的一部分看起来比另一部分更近。

collocations: a cue based on retinal disparity

words.enDefinition: Depth perception arising from differences between the two eyes' images.

examples.en: The instructor used paired pictures to illustrate stereopsis even though each picture alone looked completely flat.
examples.zh: 老师用成对图画展示「双眼立体视觉」，尽管单看每幅图都显得完全是平面的。

examples.en: The reading distinguished stereopsis from depth impressions that could arise when viewing with just one eye.
examples.zh: 阅读材料区分了「双眼立体视觉」和仅用一只眼睛观察时也能产生的深度感。

words.enDefinition: Information available to one eye that contributes to depth perception.

examples.en: The lecture treated overlap as a monocular depth cue because it remained visible in a single image.
examples.zh: 课堂把遮挡视为「单眼深度线索」，因为它在单张图像中也看得见。

examples.en: We found a monocular depth cue in the painted street before discussing the paired camera views.
examples.zh: 我们先在画中的街道上找出一种「单眼深度线索」，再讨论成对的相机视图。

words.enDefinition: Relative image motion of objects at different depths as the viewpoint changes.

examples.en: The animation demonstrated motion parallax when the near trees crossed the picture faster than the distant hills.
examples.zh: 动画展示了「运动视差」，近处树木掠过画面的速度比远处山丘快。

examples.en: The instructor used motion parallax to explain why nearby and distant objects shifted differently during the simulated movement.
examples.zh: 老师用「运动视差」解释为何在模拟移动时，近处和远处物体在视野中移动的方式不同。

words.enDefinition: A depth cue in which parallel lines project as converging with distance.

examples.en: The railroad drawing used linear perspective to make the parallel tracks appear to converge farther away.
examples.zh: 铁路图通过「线性透视」使平行的铁轨看起来在远处会合。

examples.en: We identified linear perspective in the classroom drawing by following the edges of the long tiled hallway.
examples.zh: 在课堂图画里，我们沿着长长的铺砖走廊两边看，辨认出「线性透视」。

words.enDefinition: A change in apparent texture density or scale that signals depth.

examples.en: The pebble photograph showed a texture gradient as the visible gaps narrowed toward the far end.
examples.zh: 卵石照片中的缝隙在画面远端看起来更窄，展示了「纹理梯度」。

examples.en: A texture gradient made the flat drawing of a tiled courtyard seem to extend into the distance.
examples.zh: 「纹理梯度」让平面图上铺瓷砖的庭院看起来向远处延伸。

words.enDefinition: Depth information from differences in apparent size among objects expected to be similar in size.

examples.en: The two identical benches illustrated a relative size cue when one occupied much less of the picture.
examples.zh: 两张相同的长椅中，有一张在画面上占的面积小得多，展示了「相对大小线索」。

examples.en: We explained the distance judgment using a relative size cue rather than assuming one object was smaller.
examples.zh: 我们用「相对大小线索」来解释距离判断，没有假定其中一件物体的实际尺寸较小。

collocations: an example of a relative size cue

words.enDefinition: A depth cue in which one object partly blocks another from view.

examples.en: Interposition made the partly hidden notebook look farther away than the mug in the photograph.
examples.zh: 「遮挡深度线索」让照片中被部分挡住的笔记本看起来比马克杯更远。

examples.en: The example used interposition, so students could tell which object was nearer without judging its exact distance.
examples.zh: 示例运用了「遮挡深度线索」，学生无需判断确切距离，也能分辨哪个物体更近。

collocations: use interposition as a depth cue

words.enDefinition: A depth cue based on atmospheric changes to distant objects' contrast or color.

examples.en: The painting used aerial perspective to suggest that the hazier ridge lay behind the sharper one.
examples.zh: 画作利用「空气透视」给人这样的印象，较模糊的山脊位于轮廓较清晰的山脊后方。

examples.en: The class identified aerial perspective in a photo whose distant buildings looked lower in contrast.
examples.zh: 全班在一张远处建筑对比度较低的照片中辨认出了「空气透视」。

words.enDefinition: The experience of movement without corresponding continuous physical displacement.

examples.en: The two alternating lights produced apparent motion even though neither light moved across the display.
examples.zh: 尽管两盏灯在显示器上都没有移动，它们交替亮起还是产生了「似动」。

examples.en: The tutor used apparent motion to explain why a sequence of separate still images can look continuous.
examples.zh: 辅导老师用「似动」解释为什么一连串独立静止图像可以看起来连贯运动。

words.enDefinition: A readiness to interpret ambiguous sensory input in a particular way.

examples.en: The preceding picture created a perceptual set that influenced how students interpreted the ambiguous drawing.
examples.zh: 前一幅图形成了「知觉定势」，影响学生解读含义不明确的图画。

examples.en: The class compared how a perceptual set changed after seeing different titles for the same image.
examples.zh: 全班比较了同一图像配上不同标题后，「知觉定势」发生的变化。

collocations: a perceptual set induced by context
the effects of a perceptual set

words.enDefinition: Perception shaped by prior knowledge, expectations, or the surrounding context.

examples.en: The blurry letter was easier to identify in a word, illustrating top-down processing in the lecture.
examples.zh: 模糊的字母放在完整单词中更容易认出，这是课上展示的「自上而下加工」。

examples.en: The instructor used top-down processing to explain why a meaningful sentence helped listeners interpret an unclear syllable.
examples.zh: 老师用「自上而下加工」解释为什么有明确含义的句子能帮助听者听懂含糊的音节。

words.enDefinition: Perceptual processing driven by features of incoming sensory information.

examples.en: The lecture described bottom-up processing as starting with the lines and edges visible in the unfamiliar image.
examples.zh: 课堂把「自下而上加工」描述为从陌生图像里可见的线条和边缘开始。

examples.en: We discussed bottom-up processing when the new picture offered strong visual cues but no familiar context.
examples.zh: 新图片提供了清晰的视觉线索，却缺少熟悉的背景，我们就此讨论了「自下而上加工」。

words.enDefinition: Combining information from different senses to produce a coherent percept.

examples.en: The lecture used multisensory integration to explain how listeners combined visible mouth movements with the recorded sounds.
examples.zh: 老师用「多感觉整合」解释听者如何把看到的口型与录音中的声音结合起来。

examples.en: We discussed multisensory integration after comparing how the same clip appeared with and without its soundtrack.
examples.zh: 我们比较同一片段在有无声轨时给人的印象，随后讨论了「多感觉整合」。

words.enDefinition: A shift in perceived sound location toward a visible event.

examples.en: The ventriloquism effect made the recorded voice seem to come from the moving puppet on the screen.
examples.zh: 受「腹语效应」影响，录制的人声听起来像是屏幕上活动的木偶发出的。

examples.en: The ventriloquism effect diagram marked the actual speaker and the location where listeners thought the sound originated.
examples.zh: 「腹语效应」示意图标出了扬声器的实际位置和听者以为声音传出的位置。

collocations: a demonstration of the ventriloquism effect

words.enDefinition: A change in heard speech caused by conflicting visible articulation.

examples.en: The McGurk effect appeared when the same recorded syllable sounded different after students saw another mouth movement.
examples.zh: 学生看见另一种口型后觉得同一录制音节听起来不同，出现了「麦格克效应」。

examples.en: The class compared sound-only and video versions of the clip to discuss the McGurk effect.
examples.zh: 全班比较了同一片段的纯音频和视频版本，以讨论「麦格克效应」。

collocations: a demonstration of the McGurk effect

words.enDefinition: Perceptually organizing a mixture of sounds into meaningful events or sources.

examples.en: The lecture introduced auditory scene analysis using a recording with footsteps, conversation, and a door closing.
examples.zh: 老师用一段包含脚步声、谈话声和关门声的录音介绍「听觉场景分析」。

examples.en: We discussed auditory scene analysis after identifying several distinct sources in the same synthetic recording.
examples.zh: 我们从同一段合成录音中辨认出几个不同的声源，然后讨论了「听觉场景分析」。

collocations: a demonstration of auditory scene analysis
the role of auditory scene analysis

words.enDefinition: Perceiving a mixture or sequence of sounds as separate auditory streams.

examples.en: The alternating tones illustrated auditory stream segregation when students heard two distinct sequences instead of one tune.
examples.zh: 当学生听出两个独立的声音序列而非一段旋律时，这组交替音展示了「听觉流分离」。

examples.en: The lecturer tested whether auditory stream segregation was reported for the example with more widely separated pitches.
examples.zh: 老师询问，同组音调的音高差加大后，是否有人报告听到了「听觉流分离」。

words.enDefinition: Reduced detectability of a sound due to another sound.

examples.en: The auditory masking example played a faint tone that was harder to hear against the background sound.
examples.zh: 「听觉掩蔽」示例播放了一个微弱音调，有背景声时更难听清。

examples.en: The worksheet compared auditory masking across two synthetic examples with the same target sound.
examples.zh: 习题在使用相同目标声的两个合成示例中比较了「听觉掩蔽」。

words.enDefinition: Identifying the apparent position of a sound source.

examples.en: The lecture illustrated sound localization by asking where on the screen the recorded click seemed to originate.
examples.zh: 老师问大家，录音里的咔嗒声听起来来自屏幕的什么位置，以说明「声源定位」。

examples.en: We explained the sound localization judgments using differences in the signals reaching the two simulated ears.
examples.zh: 我们用到达两只模拟耳朵的信号差异解释「声源定位」判断。

words.enDefinition: The difference in when a sound reaches the two ears.

examples.en: The model illustrated interaural time difference by showing a click reaching one ear shortly before the other.
examples.zh: 模型展示同一咔嗒声先到达一只耳朵，片刻后才到另一只，用以说明「双耳时差」。

examples.en: The class labeled the interaural time difference on two traces of the same recorded pulse.
examples.zh: 全班在同一录制脉冲的两条曲线上标出了「双耳时差」。

collocations: localization based on interaural time difference

words.enDefinition: The difference in sound level at the two ears.

examples.en: The simulated high tone showed an interaural level difference because its measured level varied between the ears.
examples.zh: 模拟高音在两耳测得的声级不同，因此存在「双耳声级差」。

examples.en: In the diagram, the interaural level difference was visible as unequal amplitudes on the two traces.
examples.zh: 图中两条曲线的振幅不同，体现了「双耳声级差」。

collocations: a cue from interaural level difference
compare interaural level difference with timing cues

words.enDefinition: Prioritizing particular information while filtering out competing information.

examples.en: The lecture illustrated selective attention with a recording in which students followed one of two voices.
examples.zh: 老师播放一段录音，让学生从两个人声中选一个专心听，以说明「选择性注意」。

examples.en: We discussed selective attention after comparing the features students noticed while focusing on different moving shapes.
examples.zh: 我们比较了学生留意不同运动图形时发现的特征，然后讨论了「选择性注意」。

words.enDefinition: Allocating attention to more than one activity or source at a time.

examples.en: The divided attention example asked students to monitor two sound streams at the same time.
examples.zh: 「分配性注意」演示要求学生同时留意两路声音。

examples.en: We compared simulated scores under divided attention with scores from each activity performed on its own.
examples.zh: 我们把「分配性注意」条件下的模拟得分与分别完成各项活动的得分作比较。

words.enDefinition: Maintaining engagement with a task or stream over an extended period.

examples.en: The sustained attention task involved watching for the same target throughout a long classroom simulation.
examples.zh: 「持续性注意」任务要求在较长的课堂模拟中始终留意同一种目标。

examples.en: The plot showed how sustained attention differed across successive blocks in the hypothetical data set.
examples.zh: 图中显示，在这组假想数据的连续几个试验区段里，「持续性注意」有何不同。

words.enDefinition: Regulating how attention is directed and maintained in service of goals.

examples.en: The example linked attentional control to staying with a goal when a competing stimulus appeared.
examples.zh: 示例把「注意控制」与竞争刺激出现时能否继续专注于当前目标联系起来。

examples.en: Our instructor discussed attentional control after showing two tasks with different demands on focus.
examples.zh: 老师展示了对专注程度要求不同的两项任务，然后讨论了「注意控制」。

words.enDefinition: The amount of information or processing that attention can support at once.

examples.en: The instructor illustrated limited attentional capacity by comparing performance with fewer and more moving shapes.
examples.zh: 老师比较同时追踪较少和较多图形时的表现，以说明「注意容量」有限。

examples.en: In the model, attentional capacity constrained the number of targets a simulated observer could track.
examples.zh: 模型中，「注意容量」限制了模拟观察者可追踪的目标数量。

words.enDefinition: A shift of attention triggered by a stimulus without deliberate selection.

examples.en: A bright flash produced attentional capture in the example even though it was irrelevant to the task.
examples.zh: 在例子里，虽然闪光与任务无关，仍然造成了「注意捕获」。

examples.en: We saw less attentional capture in the simulation when the irrelevant flash resembled the background.
examples.zh: 模拟中，无关闪光与背景相似时，发生的「注意捕获」较少。

words.enDefinition: Releasing attention from the location or object it currently selects.

examples.en: The diagram placed attentional disengagement between attending to the initial cue and selecting the next location.
examples.zh: 流程图把「注意脱离」放在关注初始线索与选择下一位置之间。

examples.en: The response times suggested slower attentional disengagement from a colored cue than from a plain marker.
examples.zh: 反应时间表明，与普通标记相比，从彩色线索上「注意脱离」需要更长时间。

words.enDefinition: Directing attention toward a location, object, or sensory event.

examples.en: The instructor explained attentional orienting by showing how a cue directed focus toward a possible target.
examples.zh: 老师展示了线索如何把注意引向可能出现目标的位置，以解释「注意定向」。

examples.en: We compared attentional orienting toward visual and auditory events in two versions of the demonstration.
examples.zh: 我们比较了演示的两个版本中，朝向视觉事件与听觉事件的「注意定向」。

collocations: a task for studying attentional orienting

words.enDefinition: Attention guided by a person's goals or expectations.

examples.en: The endogenous attention example began with an instruction to watch the left side of the screen.
examples.zh: 「内源性注意」示例先要求观察者留意屏幕左侧。

examples.en: We discussed endogenous attention when observers followed a symbolic arrow instead of reacting to a flash.
examples.zh: 观察者跟随符号箭头，而非被闪光吸引时，我们讨论了「内源性注意」。

collocations: compare endogenous attention with exogenous attention

words.enDefinition: Attention directed by an external event that attracts it.

examples.en: The lecture used an unexpected marker to show how exogenous attention could shift toward a screen location.
examples.zh: 老师用一个出乎意料的标记展示「外源性注意」如何转向屏幕上的某处。

examples.en: We discussed exogenous attention after a brief flash drew focus away from the middle of the screen.
examples.zh: 短暂的闪光把注意从屏幕中央吸引开后，我们讨论了「外源性注意」。

words.enDefinition: Directing attention without moving the eyes or other sensory organs toward the target.

examples.en: The diagram illustrated covert attention by showing a student focusing on the edge without moving their eyes.
examples.zh: 示意图中，学生眼睛没有转动，却把注意放在边缘，以此说明「内隐注意」。

examples.en: The reading described covert attention when the relevant symbol appeared away from the central fixation point.
examples.zh: 阅读材料描述了相关符号出现在中央注视点之外时的「内隐注意」。

words.enDefinition: Directing attention while visibly orienting the eyes or other sensory organs.

examples.en: The example labeled overt attention when the observer moved their eyes toward the highlighted shape.
examples.zh: 例子把观察者将目光移向高亮形状的情形标为「外显注意」。

examples.en: We watched for overt attention in the recording by noting whether gaze moved with the target.
examples.zh: 我们记录目光是否随目标而移动，据此观察录像中的「外显注意」。

words.enDefinition: Using a cue to direct attention toward a possible target location.

examples.en: The spatial cueing demonstration compared responses to targets that appeared on the left or right.
examples.zh: 「空间线索提示」演示比较了目标出现在左右两侧时的作答。

examples.en: We used the spatial cueing diagram to see which locations were indicated before the target appeared.
examples.zh: 我们查看「空间线索提示」示意图，找出目标出现前哪些位置得到了提示。

words.enDefinition: A cue correctly indicating where or when a target will appear.

examples.en: In the example, a valid cue pointed toward the same square where the target eventually appeared.
examples.zh: 例子中，「有效线索」指向的正是目标后来出现的方框。

examples.en: The worksheet compared response times after a valid cue with times when no direction was given.
examples.zh: 习题比较给出「有效线索」后与没有提供方向时的反应时间。

collocations: a trial with a valid cue
the benefit of a valid cue

words.enDefinition: A cue indicating a location or time other than the one containing the target.

examples.en: An invalid cue pointed left, but the target in the classroom animation appeared on the right.
examples.zh: 「无效线索」指向左边，但课堂动画中的目标出现在右边。

examples.en: The graph showed slower responses when an invalid cue directed attention away from the actual target.
examples.zh: 图中显示，「无效线索」把注意引离实际目标时，作答速度更慢。

collocations: a trial with an invalid cue
the cost of an invalid cue

words.enDefinition: Slower responses to targets at a recently cued location after an interval under some conditions.

examples.en: The plot illustrated inhibition of return when responses slowed at the previously cued location after a delay.
examples.zh: 图中，经过一段延迟后，对先前提示位置的反应变慢，说明了「返回抑制」。

examples.en: Our reading discussed inhibition of return as a possible bias toward looking at new locations.
examples.zh: 阅读材料认为，「返回抑制」可能使观察者更倾向于看新的位置。

collocations: a measure of inhibition of return
a task measuring inhibition of return

words.enDefinition: Looking for a target in a display that also contains other items.

examples.en: In the visual search example, students looked for a curved symbol among several straight ones.
examples.zh: 「视觉搜索」示例中，学生在几个直线符号中寻找一个弯曲符号。

examples.en: The instructor varied the number of distractors to illustrate how visual search time could change.
examples.zh: 老师改变干扰项的数量，以说明「视觉搜索」所用时间可能如何变化。

words.enDefinition: Visual search for a target defined by a single distinguishing feature.

examples.en: The feature search example asked students to find the only red circle in an otherwise green display.
examples.zh: 在「特征搜索」示例中，学生要在其余全为绿色的图中找唯一的红色圆形。

examples.en: The simulated feature search results showed little change in response time as more distractors appeared.
examples.zh: 在模拟的「特征搜索」结果里，干扰项增多后反应时间变化不大。

collocations: compare feature search with conjunction search

words.enDefinition: Visual search for a target defined by a combination of features.

examples.en: The conjunction search worksheet asked students to find a blue square among blue triangles and green squares.
examples.zh: 「联合特征搜索」习题要求学生在蓝色三角形和绿色正方形中寻找蓝色正方形。

examples.en: In the simulated conjunction search, response time increased as more distracting shapes appeared on the screen.
examples.zh: 在模拟「联合特征搜索」中，随屏幕上干扰图形增多，反应时间延长。

words.enDefinition: A change in search performance as the number of displayed items changes.

examples.en: The graph showed a set-size effect because responses became slower when more distractors appeared on the screen.
examples.zh: 图中，屏幕上的干扰项变多时反应变慢，说明存在「项目数量效应」。

examples.en: The instructor compared the set-size effect across two tasks with different ways of defining the target.
examples.zh: 老师比较了两种不同目标定义的任务中的「项目数量效应」。

collocations: a set-size effect on reaction time

words.enDefinition: The immediate salience of an item differing visibly from its surroundings.

examples.en: The pop-out effect was clear when the one yellow item stood out among identical blue items.
examples.zh: 唯一的黄色项目在相同的蓝色项目中十分醒目，「突显效应」很明显。

examples.en: We compared the pop-out effect across two displays that used different background colors in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们比较了使用不同背景颜色的两组图中的「突显效应」。

words.enDefinition: A difference in search ease when the roles of target and distractor are exchanged.

examples.en: The paired displays illustrated visual search asymmetry by switching which of the two shapes counted as the target.
examples.zh: 成对的展示图对调两种形状中的目标与干扰角色，以说明「视觉搜索不对称」。

examples.en: We found visual search asymmetry when the two reversed tasks produced different response times in the simulation.
examples.zh: 两个互换目标和干扰项的模拟任务产生了不同的反应时间，我们由此发现「视觉搜索不对称」。

collocations: an example of visual search asymmetry

words.enDefinition: Reduced ability to report a second target that closely follows a first target in a rapid stream.

examples.en: The lecture showed an attentional blink when the second target went unnoticed soon after the first.
examples.zh: 课堂演示了「注意瞬脱」，第一个目标后很快出现的第二个目标没有被注意到。

examples.en: We marked the attentional blink on the graph where reports of the second target temporarily dipped.
examples.zh: 我们在第二个目标的报告率暂时下降的图段标出「注意瞬脱」。

collocations: a measure of the attentional blink

words.enDefinition: Failure to notice a visible unexpected item while attention is directed elsewhere.

examples.en: Inattentional blindness explained why some viewers missed the extra shape while counting events elsewhere in the clip.
examples.zh: 「非注意盲视」解释了为什么一些观众在数片段中其他位置的事件时，漏看了额外图形。

examples.en: The tutor distinguished inattentional blindness from a failure to see because an item was physically hidden.
examples.zh: 辅导老师区分了「非注意盲视」与物体实际被遮住而看不见的情况。

words.enDefinition: Failure to notice a difference between successive views of a scene.

examples.en: The slide illustrated change blindness by alternating street pictures that differed in where one sign appeared.
examples.zh: 课堂投影片交替显示两张路牌位置不同的街景图，以说明「变化盲视」。

examples.en: We compared change blindness in the two versions of the demonstration with and without a brief interruption.
examples.zh: 我们比较了有无短暂间隔的两个版本中出现的「变化盲视」。

words.enDefinition: The performance difference between conflicting and matching word-meaning and ink-color conditions in the classic task.

examples.en: The Stroop effect appeared when students took longer to name conflicting ink colors on the screen.
examples.zh: 学生说出与字义冲突的墨水颜色时用时更长，出现了「斯特鲁普效应」。

examples.en: The instructor used the Stroop effect to illustrate competition between a word meaning and a color response.
examples.zh: 老师用「斯特鲁普效应」展示字义与颜色作答之间的竞争。

collocations: a classroom example of the Stroop effect

words.enDefinition: Following one voice or noticing relevant speech among competing conversations.

examples.en: The cocktail party effect helped explain why the listener followed one conversation in a crowded room.
examples.zh: 「鸡尾酒会效应」有助于解释听者为何能在拥挤的房间里听清其中一段对话。

examples.en: Our tutor illustrated the cocktail party effect with a recording containing several people speaking at once.
examples.zh: 辅导老师用一段几个人同时说话的录音说明了「鸡尾酒会效应」。

collocations: an example of the cocktail party effect

words.enDefinition: A task presenting different sounds simultaneously to the two ears.

examples.en: The dichotic listening example described different speech recordings reaching the left and right ears at once.
examples.zh: 「双耳分听」示例描述了不同的语音录音同时到达左右耳的情形。

examples.en: We discussed dichotic listening using a diagram with a separate speech stream marked for each ear.
examples.zh: 我们用一幅分别标明每只耳朵所听语音流的示意图讨论了「双耳分听」。

words.enDefinition: Repeating a stream of speech aloud as it is heard.

examples.en: In the auditory shadowing demonstration, the student repeated the selected message as the recording played.
examples.zh: 在「听觉跟述」演示中，学生边听录音边复述选中的语音。

examples.en: We compared auditory shadowing scores before discussing how much of the other message students had noticed.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「听觉跟述」得分，再讨论学生留意到了另一段语音的多少内容。

words.enDefinition: A performance cost when two activities are carried out together.

examples.en: The example showed dual-task interference when the simulated participant performed both judgments more slowly together.
examples.zh: 例子中，模拟参与者同时做两种判断时，两项都变慢了，说明存在「双任务干扰」。

examples.en: We compared each activity alone with the combined condition to estimate dual-task interference in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，我们比较各项活动单独进行与同时进行的情况，以估计「双任务干扰」。

words.enDefinition: Delayed response to the second of two tasks when their stimuli occur in close succession.

examples.en: The psychological refractory period appeared when the second response slowed as the two task signals moved closer together.
examples.zh: 两个任务信号靠得更近时，第二次反应变慢，出现了「心理不应期」效应。

examples.en: We discussed the psychological refractory period after comparing closer and wider spacing between the two signals.
examples.zh: 比较两个信号之间较短和较长的间隔后，我们讨论了「心理不应期」。

words.enDefinition: A decline in detecting occasional targets during prolonged monitoring.

examples.en: The simulated data showed a vigilance decrement as learners detected fewer rare targets later in the task.
examples.zh: 模拟数据显示，学习者在任务后段检出的少见目标更少，出现了「警觉性衰减」。

examples.en: We compared the first and last blocks to estimate the vigilance decrement in the classroom record.
examples.zh: 我们比较了课堂记录中的首个和最后一个区段，以估计「警觉性衰减」。

collocations: the size of a vigilance decrement

words.enDefinition: Keeping track of several designated moving objects among other objects.

examples.en: The multiple object tracking demonstration asked students to follow three marked dots after their labels disappeared.
examples.zh: 「多目标追踪」演示要求学生在标记消失后继续追踪原先标过的三个圆点。

examples.en: The instructor changed the number of targets to compare multiple object tracking accuracy in the simulation.
examples.zh: 老师改变了目标数量，以比较模拟「多目标追踪」的正确率。

words.enDefinition: Displaying items one after another in rapid succession, typically at one location.

examples.en: The lecturer used rapid serial visual presentation to show letters and numbers at one central location.
examples.zh: 老师用「快速序列视觉呈现」在同一个中央位置快速依次显示字母和数字。

examples.en: In rapid serial visual presentation, the entire group of symbols appeared one at a time.
examples.zh: 采用「快速序列视觉呈现」时，整组符号依次逐一出现。

collocations: a rapid serial visual presentation task
targets in rapid serial visual presentation

words.enDefinition: Reduced visibility of a target due to another visual stimulus close in time or space.

examples.en: The visual masking example showed a faint shape whose outline became harder to report amid another pattern.
examples.zh: 「视觉掩蔽」示例中，微弱形状被另一图案干扰，因此更难报告它的轮廓。

examples.en: We compared visual masking across two versions of the slide that used different surrounding patterns.
examples.zh: 我们比较了采用不同干扰图案的两版幻灯片中的「视觉掩蔽」。

words.enDefinition: Subjective awareness of inner experiences and the surrounding world.

examples.en: The opening lecture on consciousness asked why the same image can yield different reported experiences.
examples.zh: 关于「意识」的第一堂课提出了一个问题，为什么同一幅图像可以使人报告不同的体验。

examples.en: We discussed how consciousness might be studied when observers can describe what they saw themselves.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了观察者能自行描述所见时，研究者可以如何研究「意识」。

words.enDefinition: A state of awareness differing markedly from ordinary waking experience.

examples.en: The lecture considered dreaming an altered state of consciousness with experiences distinct from ordinary waking awareness.
examples.zh: 课堂把做梦视为一种「意识改变状态」，其中的体验不同于平常清醒时的感受。

examples.en: In the worksheet, students compared descriptions of an altered state of consciousness with reports of ordinary wakefulness.
examples.zh: 习题要求学生把对「意识改变状态」的描述与平常清醒时的报告作比较。

collocations: describe an altered state of consciousness
study an altered state of consciousness
an example of an altered state of consciousness

words.enDefinition: A particular experience, thought, or perception of which someone is aware.

examples.en: The content of consciousness changed in the example when the same drawing began to look like a face.
examples.zh: 例子中，同一幅图开始看起来像一张脸，观察者的「意识内容」随之改变。

examples.en: The handout described hearing a tone as a specific content of consciousness distinct from overall wakefulness.
examples.zh: 讲义用听到音调来举例说明一种具体的「意识内容」，并将它与整体清醒状态区分开来。

collocations: changes in the content of consciousness

words.enDefinition: Alternating perception when incompatible images are presented separately to the two eyes.

examples.en: Binocular rivalry was illustrated with different patterns that seemed to alternate despite staying physically unchanged.
examples.zh: 「双眼竞争」通过两种图案呈现出来，图案本身没有变化，观者却觉得它们交替出现。

examples.en: The lecture used binocular rivalry to separate changes in subjective experience from changes on the screen.
examples.zh: 老师用「双眼竞争」区分主观体验的变化与屏幕内容的变化。

words.enDefinition: A theory linking consciousness to information becoming widely available to otherwise specialized cognitive processes.

examples.en: Under global workspace theory, information about a visible symbol can become available beyond initial visual processing.
examples.zh: 按「全局工作空间理论」，可见符号的信息可以供初步视觉加工之外的其他过程使用。

examples.en: The seminar compared global workspace theory with another account of how experiences become available for report.
examples.zh: 讨论课比较了「全局工作空间理论」与另一种解释体验如何能够被报告的理论。

collocations: an account from global workspace theory
a prediction of global workspace theory

words.enDefinition: An internally generated biological rhythm with a period of about one day.

examples.en: The illustrative chart showed a circadian rhythm in alertness across a full day in the model.
examples.zh: 示意图展示了模型中一整天警觉性的「昼夜节律」。

examples.en: We distinguished circadian rhythm from fluctuations that repeated several times within a single classroom record.
examples.zh: 我们区分了「昼夜节律」和同一份课堂记录中反复出现多次的波动。

words.enDefinition: The timing of a particular point in an internal daily rhythm.

examples.en: We used circadian phase to compare the timing of peaks in two simulated daily cycles.
examples.zh: 我们用「昼夜节律相位」比较两个模拟日周期里峰值出现的时间。

examples.en: The diagram showed a later circadian phase even though the two curves had the same shape.
examples.zh: 图中两条曲线形状相同，但其中一条的「昼夜节律相位」更晚。

words.enDefinition: An individual's tendency toward earlier or later daily sleep and activity timing.

examples.en: The class compared chronotype categories using fictional profiles with different preferred times for sleep and activity.
examples.zh: 全班用偏好的睡眠与活动时间不同的虚构资料，对比了各种「昼夜节律类型」。

examples.en: In the worksheet, an earlier chronotype corresponded to a tendency toward earlier daily activity times.
examples.zh: 习题中，「昼夜节律类型」偏早的人也倾向于早些开始日间活动。

words.enDefinition: The daily pattern of alternating sleep and wakefulness.

examples.en: The diagram placed the sleep-wake cycle beside the simulated changes in alertness over one day.
examples.zh: 图中把「睡眠觉醒周期」与一天内模拟的警觉性变化并列展示。

examples.en: We used a full day of synthetic data to trace changes in the sleep-wake cycle.
examples.zh: 我们用一整天的合成数据梳理了「睡眠觉醒周期」的变化。

collocations: the timing of the sleep-wake cycle
a feature of the sleep-wake cycle

words.enDefinition: The drive for sleep that generally builds during wakefulness and declines during sleep.

examples.en: The classroom model showed homeostatic sleep pressure increasing over the simulated period of wakefulness before bedtime.
examples.zh: 课堂模型显示，睡前模拟清醒期内，「稳态睡眠压力」逐步上升。

examples.en: We compared homeostatic sleep pressure before and after the sleep interval shown on the model's graph.
examples.zh: 我们比较了模型图中睡眠时段前后的「稳态睡眠压力」。

collocations: a build-up of homeostatic sleep pressure
a model of homeostatic sleep pressure

words.enDefinition: An account combining homeostatic sleep pressure with the influence of circadian timing.
acceptedEnVariants: two process model of sleep regulation

examples.en: The two-process model of sleep regulation showed why time awake alone did not explain the simulated pattern.
examples.zh: 「睡眠调节双过程模型」说明了为什么单靠清醒时长并不能解释模拟模式。

examples.en: We drew two curves in class to represent the two-process model of sleep regulation.
examples.zh: 我们在课上画了两条曲线来表示「睡眠调节双过程模型」。

collocations: the homeostatic component of the two-process model of sleep regulation
compare predictions of the two-process model of sleep regulation
apply the two-process model of sleep regulation

words.enDefinition: The time from a specified bedtime or sleep opportunity to sleep onset.

examples.en: The worksheet measured sleep latency from the start of the observation window to the first sleep interval.
examples.zh: 习题从观察时段开始算到第一个睡眠时段，以测量「入睡潜伏期」。

examples.en: The second simulated record had a longer sleep latency even though both observation windows started together.
examples.zh: 尽管两个观察时段同时开始，第二份模拟记录的「入睡潜伏期」更长。

words.enDefinition: The total time spent awake after falling asleep and before the final awakening.

examples.en: In the classroom record, wake after sleep onset included three separate intervals before the final awakening.
examples.zh: 课堂记录里的「入睡后清醒时间」包括最后醒来之前三个彼此分开的时段。

examples.en: We summed the short awakenings in the simulated plot to find wake after sleep onset.
examples.zh: 我们把模拟图上各个短暂的清醒时段相加，算出「入睡后清醒时间」。

collocations: a measure of wake after sleep onset
compare wake after sleep onset across records

words.enDefinition: The proportion of time in bed or the recording period actually spent asleep.

examples.en: Our worksheet defined sleep efficiency as time asleep divided by total time in bed for the example.
examples.zh: 习题在这个例子中将「睡眠效率」定义为睡眠时长除以卧床总时长。

examples.en: The two fictional charts showed different sleep efficiency despite recording the same total time in bed.
examples.zh: 两张虚构图表记录的卧床总时长相同，但显示的「睡眠效率」不同。

words.enDefinition: The overall pattern and distribution of sleep stages across a sleep period.

examples.en: We compared sleep architecture in two simulated nights that had the same total amount of sleep.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两夜模拟记录的「睡眠结构」，它们的总睡眠时长相同。

examples.en: The lecture illustrated sleep architecture by plotting changes in stage across the complete fictional recording.
examples.zh: 老师把整份虚构记录中的阶段变化绘成图，以展示「睡眠结构」。

words.enDefinition: A recurring progression through non-REM and REM stages during a sleep period.

examples.en: The classroom chart showed one sleep cycle in detail before turning to the remaining night.
examples.zh: 课堂图表先详细展示了一个「睡眠周期」，然后才展示当晚的其余时段。

examples.en: We traced a sleep cycle by following the sequence of stages on the simulated graph.
examples.zh: 我们沿着模拟图上的阶段顺序，梳理了一个「睡眠周期」。

words.enDefinition: A sleep stage characterized by rapid eye movements and low skeletal muscle tone.

examples.en: The class shaded the intervals of REM sleep in the fictional overnight chart with a single color.
examples.zh: 全班用同一种颜色标出虚构的整夜图表中「快速眼动睡眠」的各个时段。

examples.en: The lecture compared REM sleep with other stages and noted that dreams can occur outside it.
examples.zh: 老师比较了「快速眼动睡眠」与其他阶段，并指出其他阶段也可能做梦。

words.enDefinition: Sleep outside the REM stage, classified into N1, N2, and N3.

examples.en: The teaching diagram used three separate labels for the stages of non-REM sleep in the example.
examples.zh: 教学示意图为示例中的「非快速眼动睡眠」三个阶段分别设置了标签。

examples.en: We tallied time in non-REM sleep before comparing it with the shorter intervals in the other category.
examples.zh: 我们先统计「非快速眼动睡眠」的时长，再与另一类中较短的时段对照。

words.enDefinition: The lightest non-REM stage, marking the transition from wakefulness into sleep.

examples.en: The classroom chart marked N1 sleep where the simulated record first shifted from wakefulness into sleep.
examples.zh: 课堂图表在模拟记录第一次从清醒转入睡眠的位置标出了「非快速眼动一期睡眠」。

examples.en: We distinguished N1 sleep from the later stage marked by spindles in the fictional overnight record.
examples.zh: 我们在虚构的整夜记录中区分了「非快速眼动一期睡眠」与有纺锤波的后续阶段。

words.enDefinition: The non-REM stage marked by sleep spindles or K-complexes under standard scoring.

examples.en: The example marked N2 sleep where the simulated record showed a spindle after the earlier stage.
examples.zh: 示例在前一阶段结束后出现纺锤波的模拟记录部分标出了「非快速眼动二期睡眠」。

examples.en: We checked which characteristic waveform supported the classroom label for N2 sleep in the sample.
examples.zh: 我们核对样本中的哪种特征波形为课堂标注「非快速眼动二期睡眠」提供了依据。

words.enDefinition: The deepest non-REM stage, characterized by prominent slow brain waves.

examples.en: The synthetic trace showed the slow waves used to identify N3 sleep in the class exercise.
examples.zh: 合成波形展示了课上用于辨认「非快速眼动三期睡眠」的慢波。

examples.en: We marked the periods of N3 sleep on the chart before looking at the stage distribution.
examples.zh: 我们先在图表上标出「非快速眼动三期睡眠」的各个时段，再查看睡眠阶段的分布。

words.enDefinition: A brief burst of rhythmic brain activity commonly seen during N2 sleep.

examples.en: The instructor circled a sleep spindle because the short rhythmic burst stood out from the surrounding trace.
examples.zh: 老师圈出了「睡眠纺锤波」，因为这段短暂的节律波在周围记录中很突出。

examples.en: We compared a sleep spindle with a slower waveform on the synthetic classroom recording.
examples.zh: 我们将课堂合成记录中的「睡眠纺锤波」与一种更慢的波形作比较。

collocations: the shape of a sleep spindle

words.enDefinition: A distinctive large brain wave commonly associated with N2 sleep.

examples.en: Our tutor labeled the K-complex on a synthetic trace next to a clearly different rhythmic burst.
examples.zh: 辅导老师在合成波形上标出「K复合波」，旁边是一段明显不同的节律波。

examples.en: The worksheet asked whether the marked feature was a K-complex or part of the background activity.
examples.zh: 习题问，标出的特征是「K复合波」还是背景活动的一部分。

words.enDefinition: A dream in which the dreamer realizes they are dreaming.

examples.en: The fictional report described a lucid dream in which someone realized they were dreaming before waking up.
examples.zh: 虚构报告描述了一个「清醒梦」，做梦者醒来之前就意识到自己正在做梦。

examples.en: We distinguished a lucid dream from an unusually vivid dream in the classroom discussion of awareness.
examples.zh: 在课堂上讨论觉察时，我们区分了「清醒梦」与异常逼真的梦。

collocations: a report of a lucid dream
the experience of a lucid dream

words.enDefinition: Remembering part or all of a dream after waking up.

examples.en: The fictional participant remembered only a setting, so the worksheet recorded partial dream recall after awakening.
examples.zh: 虚构参与者只记得一个场景，习题便把这记为醒来后出现了部分「梦境回忆」。

examples.en: We discussed dream recall when two fictional participants described different amounts of detail after waking up.
examples.zh: 两位虚构参与者醒来后描述的细节多少不同，我们就此讨论了「梦境回忆」。

words.enDefinition: A graph showing how sleep stages change over a recording.

examples.en: The lecturer used a hypnogram to show how sleep stages changed across the fictional night.
examples.zh: 老师用「睡眠分期图」展示了虚构的一整夜中睡眠阶段如何变化。

examples.en: We read the time axis of the hypnogram before comparing the duration of the marked stages.
examples.zh: 我们先看「睡眠分期图」的时间轴，再比较标出的各阶段的持续时间。

words.enDefinition: Temporary grogginess or reduced alertness immediately after waking from sleep.

examples.en: The example described sleep inertia as a short period of reduced alertness after the fictional participant woke.
examples.zh: 示例把「睡眠惯性」描述为虚构参与者醒来后警觉性暂时较低的一小段时间。

examples.en: We discussed sleep inertia when the simulated scores improved across the first several observations after waking.
examples.zh: 模拟得分在醒来后的前几次观察中逐步提高，我们就此讨论了「睡眠惯性」。
